A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same FastLongSpeech work. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices are readable and support reliable comparison, including matching retained content across pagination changes.

before.justification: v1 reports original speech-task evaluations, component ablations, and computational-efficiency measurements in Sections 4–5 and Appendices E–F.

after.justification: v2 retains those original results and adds cascaded-baseline, SPIRAL-H retrieval, and context-length experiments in Table 4 and Appendices F–G.

M1.justification: The architecture, CTC-based content density, iterative fusion procedure, and two-stage dynamic compression training remain unchanged. The added context-length experiments evaluate the existing method without introducing a new component.

E1.justification: Section 4.1 and Appendix F add evaluation on SPIRAL-H for long-speech information retrieval. This extends the existing speech-task coverage with one related task and benchmark; training datasets and previous evaluation coverage are retained.

E2.justification: Table 4 adds a cascaded Whisper-Large-V3 plus Qwen-7B-Chat comparator to the long-speech comparison. Table 10 introduces an evaluated SpeechPrune comparison; v1 only discussed that method in related work. These are targeted additions, with the previous comparator sets retained.

E3.justification: New evaluations include a LongSpeech-Eval sweep over L=200, 400, 750, 1200, and 4000, and SPIRAL-H accuracy comparisons at similar pruning rates. These extend the evaluation design; previously reported splits, training settings, and scoring procedures are unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendix G adds a context-length sensitivity analysis, testing performance within and beyond the training range. Existing component ablations, compression analyses, and applications to vanilla models remain unchanged.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests for its experiments. The added results continue the existing point-estimate reporting practice.

E6.justification: Original results are retained, with localized additions. Table 4 adds Cascaded at score 3.75 and runtime 17.23+1.38 seconds, versus the retained FastLongSpeech values of 3.55 and 1.47 seconds. Table 10 reports 76.81% accuracy at 65.88% pruning for FastLongSpeech versus SpeechPrune's 63.77% at 60.00%. Table 11 adds context-length results, including 3.66 at L=1200 and 3.59 at L=4000.

T1.justification: Equations 1–7 and the mathematical definitions of content density, frame similarity, fusion lengths, and training losses are retained. No new formal assumptions, propositions, proofs, or derivations are introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same central contributions: efficient long-speech processing using short-speech training, iterative fusion, dynamic compression training, and LongSpeech-Eval. Additional experiments do not redefine these claims.

C2.justification: Appendix G newly interprets performance at L=1200 as generalization beyond training and attributes the decline at L=4000 to lack of exposure to long contexts. Section 5.2 also adds an efficiency interpretation against the cascaded baseline. The original limitations paragraph is unchanged.

D1.justification: v2 specifies the models composing the new cascaded baseline and adds a SPIRAL dataset access link in Appendix F. The existing code link, implementation descriptions, and Table 6 hyperparameters remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds Llama-Omni2 and two simultaneous-translation citations, plus a brief StreamUni discussion. Overall positioning is retained. SpeechPrune was already cited; v2 duplicates its bibliography entry as reference 42, which the new StreamUni sentence also incorrectly cites.

P1.justification: Most prose and section organization are retained. Local additions describe the new evaluations, introduce Appendix G and acknowledgements, and update the publication footer and code-footnote marker. There is no extensive rewriting or narrative restructuring.

P2.justification: v2 expands Table 4 with a cascaded-baseline row and adds Tables 10–11. Existing tables and the evaluation-template figure undergo modest reflow. The architecture diagram and performance plots are visually unchanged.

improvement.justification: The additional retrieval benchmark, cascaded comparator, and context-length analysis modestly strengthen the empirical evidence and clarify efficiency and generalization tradeoffs absent from v1. However, Section 4.3 retains optimal-performance wording without reconciling the cascaded baseline's higher score in Table 4, and the new StreamUni discussion has a citation mismatch. The net improvement is useful but limited.
